new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Checked on the page images (printed p. 28) and printed p. 29) of Blench 2003, plus the scanned text p. 28 §3.3 Tones reads: "All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones and this can therefore be posited in Proto-Ron. Tones have significant grammatical functions as well as lexical –for example making plurals or deriving verbs from nouns." The only difference from the reported quote is the dash (printed as an en-dash with no following space; reported as em-dash with spaces). p. 29 reads exactly: "The falling tone in Sha and Karfa also suggests that the original tone was *láhyàl and that the tones coalesced after a long internal vowel became short." The p. 29…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Duhwa/Karfa, like every attested Ron lect, is a tone language with three level tones plus contour ('combination') tones; tone is lexically and grammatically contrastive, and Karfa has falling tones that arose historically from coalescence of two tones after a long internal vowel shortened (Karfa 'to call' yâ:l < *láhyàl). No opened source says anything about word stress or accent: none gives a stress position and none says stress is absent.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. On tone: Karfa (and Sha) falling tones are explained as historical tone coalescence (p. 29); Decker et al. 2021 warn that their tone transcriptions are preliminary and unanalysed (App. E p. 32).
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level comparative statement about the Ron lexicon (word-level lexical and grammatical tone on citation forms from wordlists), not a word-prosody description of Duhwa specifically; the p. 29 sentence names Karfa explicitly. Decker et al. 2021 and the Blench wordlist give only tone-marked citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog duhw1236 'Duhwa' is the language the older literature calls Karfa/Kerifa (Blench 2003, Blench's Ron comparative wordlist, Blench's Atlas entry 243) after the village Karfa; Decker et al. 2021 §5.1.1 report the autonym Duhwa [dùhʷà] and locate Karfa village (hamlets Ahum and Tisheu) in Bokkos LGA, Plateau State (the Atlas's 'Nasarawa State, Akwanga LGA' is wrong). Blench 2003 p. 28 is a statement about all Ron lects (ronn1241, fyer1238, shaa1241, kule1250, mund1334, Duhwa, etc.); only the p. 29 sentence names Karfa specifically. Closest sister is Mundat/Mindat (mund1334), with which Duhwa forms Glottolog's 'Mundaic'.

Nothing anywhere…

sources.note: §8.2 'Phonetic inventories of Duhwa, Mindat, and Sya' pp. 17-18 gives only a cursory consonant chart, five vowels with apparent VV sequences, prenasalised/labialised/palatalised consonants and a plural suffix -ak; Appendix E p. 32: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Appendix E-F pp. 33-46: 348-item Duhwa (Karfa) wordlist with tone diacritics, elicited 11 Feb 2020 from a 55-year-old man. §5.1.1 p. 9: autonym Duhwa [dùhʷà], Karfa is the village name. Nothing on stress or accent.
